argument: A reduction transforms instances of problem $A$ into problem $B$ while preserving answers. If $A$ is hard and reduces efficiently to $B$, then $B$ is at least as hard; completeness organizes broad classes around representative problems.
boundary: The reduction type determines what transfers.
Worst-case hardness does not imply every instance is difficult.
A reduction can introduce impractical constants or destroy domain structure.
claim: A reduction transforms instances of problem $A$ into problem $B$ while preserving answers. If $A$ is hard and reduces efficiently to $B$, then $B$ is at least as hard; completeness organizes broad classes around representative problems.
interpretation: Principia should record the direction and cost of a reduction. Superficial similarity between tasks is not a complexity reduction.

argument: A principal delegating work to an agent cannot generally condition rewards on hidden effort or all relevant actions. When the agent’s objective differs from the principal’s, contracts must trade incentive strength against risk sharing, measurement noise, gaming, and monitoring cost.
boundary: The result changes when effort is observable, objectives are aligned, or repeated reputation disciplines behavior.
Performance measures can induce multitask distortion and Goodhart effects.
High-powered incentives may shift risk to parties least able to bear it.
claim: A principal delegating work to an agent cannot generally condition rewards on hidden effort or all relevant actions. When the agent’s objective differs from the principal’s, contracts must trade incentive strength against risk sharing, measurement noise, gaming, and monitoring cost.
interpretation: Agentic AI systems make hidden-action problems concrete. More monitoring is not automatically optimal if it displaces useful autonomy or encourages metric gaming.
